q15.

The repository maps these tables with hand-written SQL (there is no ORM/`TableName()` method), so the mapping is between the domain structs in `store/` and the `INSERT INTO`/`SELECT ... FROM` statements in the per-dialect drivers under `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/`.

| Table | Struct — path |
| --- | --- |
| `user` | `User` — `store/user.go` (line 29) |
| `attachment` | `Attachment` — `store/attachment.go` (line 16) |
| `reaction` | `Reaction` — `store/reaction.go` (line 7) |

Supporting evidence from the SQLite driver, where each struct is written to its table:

```17:17:store/db/sqlite/user.go
	stmt := "INSERT INTO user (" + strings.Join(fields, ", ") + ") VALUES (" + strings.Join(placeholder, ", ") + ") RETURNING id, description, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status"
```

```34:34:store/db/sqlite/attachment.go
	stmt := "INSERT INTO `attachment` (" + strings.Join(fields, ", ") + ") VALUES (" + strings.Join(placeholder, ", ") + ") RETURNING `id`, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`"
```

```16:16:store/db/sqlite/reaction.go
	stmt := "INSERT INTO `reaction` (" + strings.Join(fields, ", ") + ") VALUES (" + strings.Join(placeholder, ", ") + ") RETURNING `id`, `created_ts`"
```

The MySQL and Postgres drivers have parallel files (`store/db/mysql/user.go`, `store/db/mysql/attachment.go`, `store/db/postgres/attachment.go`, etc.) using the same table names for the same structs.
